<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
  xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/maven-v4_0_0.xsd">
  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

  <parent>
    <groupId>com.google.auto</groupId>
    <artifactId>auto-parent</artifactId>
    <version>3</version>
  </parent>

  <artifactId>auto-common</artifactId>
  <version>1.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
  <name>Auto Common Libraries</name>
  <description>
    Common utilities for creating annotation processors.
  </description>

  <scm>
    <url>http://github.com/google/auto</url>
    <connection>scm:git:git://github.com/google/auto.git</connection>
    <developerConnection>scm:git:ssh://git@github.com/google/auto.git</developerConnection>
    <tag>HEAD</tag>
  </scm>

  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
      <artifactId>guava</artifactId>
      <version>18.0</version>
    </dependency>
    <!-- test dependencies -->
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
      <artifactId>guava-testlib</artifactId>
      <version>18.0</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
      <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
      <version>0.7</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>junit</groupId>
      <artifactId>junit</artifactId>
      <version>4.11</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.truth</groupId>
      <artifactId>truth</artifactId>
      <version>0.25</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>

  <build>
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.5</version>
      </plugin>
    </plugins>
  </build>
</project>

# POM File Analysis

This is a Maven parent POM for Google's Auto project (code generators for Java).

## Key Findings:

**No direct dependencies on com.sun:tools** are declared in the `<dependencies>` section of this file.

**Tools.jar handling via profiles:**

The POM includes two profiles that reference tools.jar:

1. **default-profile** (active by default):
   - Checks for existence: `${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar`
   - Sets property: `<toolsjar>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</toolsjar>`

2. **mac-profile** (inactive by default):
   - Checks for existence: `${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar`
   - Sets property: `<toolsjar>${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar</toolsjar>`

These profiles conditionally set the `toolsjar` property based on the JDK environment, allowing child modules to reference tools.jar as needed without explicitly declaring a dependency in this parent POM. The actual dependency would likely be declared in child modules using the `${toolsjar}` property.

2. Add a profile in the submodule POMs to provide the `${toolsjar}` property for JDK 9+ that points to a non-existent file but with a condition that makes the dependency optional

# Build Failure Analysis - Google Auto Project

## Repository: google/auto

## Error Summary
All submodules fail to build with the error:
```
Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar
```

## Root Cause
The project uses the `compile-testing` library for annotation processor testing. The versions used
(0.6, 0.7, 0.8) declare a mandatory dependency on `com.sun:tools` with a system path to `tools.jar`.

In JDK 8 and earlier, `tools.jar` existed at `$JAVA_HOME/lib/tools.jar` and contained the
annotation processing API. Starting from JDK 9, `tools.jar` was removed - the annotation
processing API is now part of the JDK module system (`java.compiler` module).

Since the build environment uses JDK 11 (OpenJDK 11.0.27), the `tools.jar` file does not exist,
causing the dependency resolution to fail.

## Affected Files and Versions
1. common/pom.xml - compile-testing:0.7
2. factory/pom.xml - compile-testing:0.8
3. service/pom.xml - compile-testing:0.6
4. value/pom.xml - compile-testing:0.6

## Solution
Upgrade `compile-testing` dependency to version 0.15 or later in all affected POM files.

In version 0.15+, the `com.sun:tools` dependency is moved inside a Maven profile that only
activates when `${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar` exists. This means:
- On JDK 8: Profile activates, tools.jar is used
- On JDK 9+: Profile does not activate, dependency is not added (not needed since API is in JDK)

## Changes Required
1. common/pom.xml: Change compile-testing version from 0.7 to 0.15
2. factory/pom.xml: Change compile-testing version from 0.8 to 0.15
3. service/pom.xml: Change compile-testing version from 0.6 to 0.15
4. value/pom.xml: Change compile-testing version from 0.6 to 0.15

## Error Type
Build configuration error - incompatible dependency version with JDK 11

All submodules fail to build with the error:
```
Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar
```

## Root Cause
The project uses the `compile-testing` library for annotation processor testing. The versions used
(0.6, 0.7, 0.8) declare a mandatory dependency on `com.sun:tools` with a system path to `tools.jar`.

In JDK 8 and earlier, `tools.jar` existed at `$JAVA_HOME/lib/tools.jar` and contained the
annotation processing API. Starting from JDK 9, `tools.jar` was removed - the annotation
processing API is now part of the JDK module system (`java.compiler` module).

Since the build environment uses JDK 11 (OpenJDK 11.0.27), the `tools.jar` file does not exist,
causing the dependency resolution to fail.

## Affected Files and Versions
1. common/pom.xml - compile-testing:0.7
2. factory/pom.xml - compile-testing:0.8
3. service/pom.xml - compile-testing:0.6
4. value/pom.xml - compile-testing:0.6

## Solution
Upgrade `compile-testing` dependency to version 0.15 or later in all affected POM files.

In version 0.15+, the `com.sun:tools` dependency is moved inside a Maven profile that only
activates when `${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar` exists. This means:
- On JDK 8: Profile activates, tools.jar is used
- On JDK 9+: Profile does not activate, dependency is not added (not needed since API is in JDK)

## Changes Required
1. common/pom.xml: Change compile-testing version from 0.7 to 0.15
2. factory/pom.xml: Change compile-testing version from 0.8 to 0.15
3. service/pom.xml: Change compile-testing version from 0.6 to 0.15
4. value/pom.xml: Change compile-testing version from 0.6 to 0.15

## Error Type
Build configuration error - incompatible dependency version with JDK 11

In 0.19, the tools dependency is inside profiles that only activate when the file exists. Since on JDK 9+, tools.jar doesn't exist, the profile won't activate and the dependency won't be added.

The issue is that 0.19 requires guava 30.0-jre and truth 0.43 which creates compatibility issues with the older guava 18.0 and truth 0.25 used by this project.

The best approach is to update both:
1. `compile-testing` to version 0.19 (which has tools in profiles)
2. `truth` to a compatible version (0.43 or later)
3. `guava` to a compatible version (30.0 or keep current and exclude guava from compile-testing)

# Build Failure Analysis - Google Auto Project

## Repository: google/auto

## Error Summary
All submodules fail to build with the error:
```
Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar
```

## Root Cause
The project uses the `compile-testing` library for annotation processor testing. The versions used
(0.6, 0.7, 0.8) declare a mandatory dependency on `com.sun:tools` with a system path to `tools.jar`.

In JDK 8 and earlier, `tools.jar` existed at `$JAVA_HOME/lib/tools.jar` and contained the
annotation processing API. Starting from JDK 9, `tools.jar` was removed - the annotation
processing API is now part of the JDK module system (`java.compiler` module).

Since the build environment uses JDK 11 (OpenJDK 11.0.27), the `tools.jar` file does not exist,
causing the dependency resolution to fail.

## Affected Files and Versions
1. common/pom.xml - compile-testing:0.7
2. factory/pom.xml - compile-testing:0.8
3. service/pom.xml - compile-testing:0.6
4. value/pom.xml - compile-testing:0.6

## Solution
Upgrade `compile-testing` dependency to version 0.15 or later in all affected POM files.

In version 0.15+, the `com.sun:tools` dependency is moved inside a Maven profile that only
activates when `${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar` exists. This means:
- On JDK 8: Profile activates, tools.jar is used
- On JDK 9+: Profile does not activate, dependency is not added (not needed since API is in JDK)

## Changes Required
1. common/pom.xml: Change compile-testing version from 0.7 to 0.15
2. factory/pom.xml: Change compile-testing version from 0.8 to 0.15
3. service/pom.xml: Change compile-testing version from 0.6 to 0.15
4. value/pom.xml: Change compile-testing version from 0.6 to 0.15

## Error Type
Build configuration error - incompatible dependency version with JDK 11

# Build Failure Analysis - Google Auto Project

## Repository: google/auto

## Error Summary
All submodules fail to build with the error:
```
Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar
```

Additionally, factory and value modules fail with:
```
cannot find symbol: class Generated, location: package javax.annotation
```

## Root Cause Analysis

### Issue 1: tools.jar Dependency (Primary)
The project uses the `compile-testing` library for annotation processor testing. The versions used
(0.6, 0.7, 0.8) declare a mandatory dependency on `com.sun:tools` with a system path to `tools.jar`.

In JDK 8 and earlier, `tools.jar` existed at `$JAVA_HOME/lib/tools.jar` and contained the
annotation processing API. Starting from JDK 9, `tools.jar` was removed - the annotation
processing API is now part of the JDK module system (`java.compiler` module).

Since the build environment uses JDK 11 (OpenJDK 11.0.27), the `tools.jar` file does not exist,
causing the dependency resolution to fail.

### Issue 2: javax.annotation.Generated (Secondary)
The `javax.annotation.Generated` annotation was removed from the JDK in Java 9+. It was part of
Java EE which was deprecated in JDK 9 and removed in JDK 11. The factory and value modules use
this annotation for code generation marking.

### Issue 3: Truth API Changes (Tertiary)
Upgrading compile-testing to 0.18 brings in Truth 0.44 which has API changes:
- `hasMessage(String)` was replaced with `hasMessageThat().isEqualTo(String)`

## Affected Files

### POM Files
1. common/pom.xml - compile-testing:0.7, truth:0.25, junit:4.11
2. factory/pom.xml - compile-testing:0.8, truth:0.25, uses javax.annotation.Generated
3. service/pom.xml - compile-testing:0.6, truth:0.24, junit:4.11
4. value/pom.xml - compile-testing:0.6, truth:0.25, junit:4.11, uses javax.annotation.Generated

### Source Files
1. common/src/test/java/com/google/auto/common/AnnotationMirrorsTest.java - uses deprecated Truth API

## Solution Applied

### Fix 1: Upgrade compile-testing to 0.18
In version 0.18, the `com.sun:tools` dependency is moved inside a Maven profile that only
activates when `${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar` exists. This means:
- On JDK 8: Profile activates, tools.jar is used
- On JDK 9+: Profile does not activate, dependency is not added (not needed since API is in JDK)

### Fix 2: Add javax.annotation-api dependency
Added `javax.annotation:javax.annotation-api:1.3.2` to factory and value modules to provide
the `javax.annotation.Generated` annotation that was removed from the JDK.

### Fix 3: Upgrade Truth and JUnit
- Upgraded truth from 0.24/0.25 to 0.44 (required by compile-testing 0.18)
- Upgraded junit from 4.11 to 4.12 (required by compile-testing 0.18)

### Fix 4: Update Test Code
- Changed `assertThat(e).hasMessage(...)` to `assertThat(e).hasMessageThat().isEqualTo(...)`
  in AnnotationMirrorsTest.java to match the new Truth API.

## Patch Files Created
1. patch_1.diff - common/pom.xml dependency updates
2. patch_2.diff - AnnotationMirrorsTest.java Truth API fix
3. patch_3.diff - service/pom.xml dependency updates
4. patch_4.diff - factory/pom.xml dependency updates + javax.annotation-api
5. patch_5.diff - value/pom.xml dependency updates + javax.annotation-api

## Error Type
Build configuration error - incompatible dependency versions with JDK 11

## Verification
All modules now compile successfully:
- common: BUILD SUCCESS
- service: BUILD SUCCESS
- factory: BUILD SUCCESS
- value: BUILD SUCCESS

# Build Failure Analysis - Google Auto Project

## Repository: google/auto

## Error Summary
All submodules fail to build with the error:
```
Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar
```

## Root Cause
The project uses the `compile-testing` library for annotation processor testing. The versions used
(0.6, 0.7, 0.8) declare a mandatory dependency on `com.sun:tools` with a system path to `tools.jar`.

In JDK 8 and earlier, `tools.jar` existed at `$JAVA_HOME/lib/tools.jar` and contained the
annotation processing API. Starting from JDK 9, `tools.jar` was removed - the annotation
processing API is now part of the JDK module system (`java.compiler` module).

Since the build environment uses JDK 11 (OpenJDK 11.0.27), the `tools.jar` file does not exist,
causing the dependency resolution to fail.

## Affected Files and Versions
1. common/pom.xml - compile-testing:0.7
2. factory/pom.xml - compile-testing:0.8
3. service/pom.xml - compile-testing:0.6
4. value/pom.xml - compile-testing:0.6

## Solution
Upgrade `compile-testing` dependency to version 0.15 or later in all affected POM files.

In version 0.15+, the `com.sun:tools` dependency is moved inside a Maven profile that only
activates when `${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar` exists. This means:
- On JDK 8: Profile activates, tools.jar is used
- On JDK 9+: Profile does not activate, dependency is not added (not needed since API is in JDK)

## Changes Required
1. common/pom.xml: Change compile-testing version from 0.7 to 0.15
2. factory/pom.xml: Change compile-testing version from 0.8 to 0.15
3. service/pom.xml: Change compile-testing version from 0.6 to 0.15
4. value/pom.xml: Change compile-testing version from 0.6 to 0.15

## Error Type
Build configuration error - incompatible dependency version with JDK 11
